IBNKATHIR-FULL (أبو جعفر محمد بن علي الباقر): A report says the angel al-Sijill saw Adam’s creation and future in the Preserved Book and told Harut and Marut, who spoke out of superiority over the angels. ALUSI-FULL (قيل): One view says the angels learned of human corruption from the Preserved Tablet; al-Alusi objects that this leaves their question unanswered and needs a strained reply. KURANYOLU-TEFSIR (author): One proposed explanation is that the angels learned about human wrongdoing from the Preserved Tablet, where future events are recorded. KASHSHAF-FULL (author): The angels may have learned of the corruption from God’s disclosure or from the Preserved Tablet. RAZI-FULL (الملائكة): They may have read the Preserved Tablet, where events through the Resurrection had been written. NASAFI-FULL (author): The angels knew through God’s information, the Preserved Tablet, or analogy between the two kinds of beings."}, {"id": "2:30/q31/p2", "position": "God had informed them", "reasons": "TAB-FULL (الحسن وقتادة): Al-Hasan and Qatada report that God told the angels he would act, gave them some knowledge but withheld other knowledge, and they asked on the basis of what they had been taught, knowing bloodshed was a grave sin. WAHIDI-BASIT (الزجاج): Al-Zajjaj transmits an unnamed explanation: God told angels humanity would corrupt and shed blood; they asked why, expecting creatures to glorify and purify God like them, and the disclosure confirmed divine knowledge of the unseen. TABRISI (author): The khalifa is Adam, God's deputy on earth who judges justly; Ibn Abbas and Ibn Masud say God informed the angels that some descendants would corrupt. TABRISI (ابن عباس وابن مسعود): Ibn Abbas and Ibn Masud report that God told angels about future sinful descendants; He disclosed the unseen and events later confirmed His report. RAZI-FULL (ابن مسعود وناس من الصحابة): One certainty report says God told angels the successor's descendants would corrupt, envy, and kill. QURTUBI-FULL (ابن زيد): Ibn Zayd and others say God informed the angels that Adam's descendants would corrupt and shed blood, so they expressed astonishment at appointing one who would disobey despite God's favor, or at the disobedience itself, or magnified both matters. ALUSI-FULL (author): The angels' judgment that humans would corrupt and shed blood need not claim knowledge of the unseen or conjecture: God informed them, as the divine reply implies, and the Qur'an omits the explicit explanation. IBNASHUR-FULL (بعض المفسرين): Some commentators proposed that God informed the angels of human traits or showed them the Preserved Tablet; Ibn ʿĀshūr says his explanation makes this speculation unnecessary."}, {"id": "2:30/q31/p3", "position": "The angels inferred it from embodied human nature", "reasons": "RAZI-FULL (author): Another conjecture was that the four humors produce appetite and anger, leading to corruption and bloodshed. IBNKATHIR-FULL (author): Ibn Kathir says the khalifa is apparently not Adam alone: the angels' prediction of corruption and bloodshed concerns a human kind, and he presents possible grounds for their knowledge, including special information, human nature, or analogy with prior inhabitants. IBNASHUR-FULL (author): The angels knew that God's purpose in creating the earth was its order and reform, learned through revelation, the nature of vicegerency, or signs of God's care and intent that it endure."}, {"id": "2:30/q31/p4", "position": "God had disclosed future corruption to the angels", "reasons": "KASHSHAF-FULL (author): God informed the angels beforehand so they would ask and receive an explanation of the wisdom, preventing doubts when the appointment occurred.
